result.summary: Propagates failure from validation's InvalidateBlock back to the invalidateblock RPC call. It ensures the RPC returns an error if a block cannot be disconnected or invalidated instead of reporting success.
result.problem: The invalidateblock RPC can report success even when a block fails to disconnect or invalidate, silently misleading node operators and test harnesses about the chain state.
evidence: Issue #36546 title: "rpc: invalidateblock reports success when a block can't be disconnected"
result.scope_notes: Diff is omitted from the input; changes span 4 files (+71/-6), likely touching validation logic and RPC dispatch.
result.card: Makes the invalidateblock RPC return an error when a block fails to be disconnected or invalidated. Currently, invalidateblock can report success even when block disconnection fails, silently leaving the chain state unchanged contrary to what callers expect (issue #36546). The fix ensures validation failure status is accurately propagated to RPC callers.
uncertainties: The exact failure conditions and specific validation error propagation mechanism cannot be verified without the diff and linked issue body.

risk.why: Incorrect handling of block invalidation failures could mask validation errors or corrupt block disconnection state handling.
